claims.call: The Maple Leafs’ power play creates at least their usual 7.9 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Maple Leafs’ power play is near the top of the league, and the Islanders’ kill is one of the worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Islanders more than most.

claims.head: Active D against forward-led
claims.body: The Islanders’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Maple Leafs’ not so much. The Islanders are the league’s best for shots from defensemen, and Toronto is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Watch the Islanders’ defensemen jump into the play.

notes.text: Mathew Barzal is on the injured non-roster list (knee injury) and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Victor Eklund has taken his spot beside Brayden Schenn and Calum Ritchie.
Kyle Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, down from 37% last season.
Chris Tanev is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Darren Raddysh has taken his spot beside Jake McCabe.
John Tavares is out week to week (lower body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Marshall Rifai was added to the roster on Oct 12.

TOR.head: Anybody’s game
TOR.body: The Islanders have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, while Toronto will be without Tavares. Then again, the Islanders will be without Barzal, and Toronto has home-ice advantage. The Maple Leafs can tip it if their power play gets going.

NYI.head: Too close to call
NYI.body: The Islanders have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, while Toronto will be without Tavares. Then again, the Islanders will be without Barzal, and Toronto has home-ice advantage. For the Islanders, the difference could be keeping shots to a minimum.

story.head: The Maple Leafs’ power play has a target
paras: The Maple Leafs won the first meeting this season, 2-1 in Toronto. The Islanders come in at 3-3-1, the Leafs at 3-3-2.
The Maple Leafs’ power play has a soft target in the Islanders’ kill. The Islanders’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Maple Leafs’ not so much.

items.text: Brayden Schenn is two goals from 300.
Emil Heineman has a point in five straight games against Toronto, with a goal in each of the last four.
The Islanders have been without Mathew Barzal all season.
The Maple Leafs are newly without Chris Tanev and John Tavares.
